title: Win-back journey
description: A segment of customers who used to buy but have not ordered in 90 days, and a two-message journey that asks what changed and offers a way back.

parameters.label: Purpose
parameters.description: The purpose key for the win-back messages; it must include the e-mail channel.

parameters.label: Offer code
parameters.description: A short code the second e-mail can mention, e.g. COMEBACK10. Use an empty string for no offer.

parameters.label: Wait between messages
parameters.description: An ISO 8601 duration such as P5D.

prerequisites.description: An enabled e-mail provider for marketing mail
A configured purpose with the e-mail channel

docs:
## Who enters

A dynamic segment: consent for the purpose, an `Order Completed` event in the last year, and none in the last 90 days. Membership is evaluated when the segment recomputes, and the journey trigger enters people when they join it.

## Before publishing

- Publish the segment first; the journey trigger needs a published segment.
- Publish both templates, then the journey (or submit all four together).
- `reentry: after_exit` lets a person come back if they leave the segment and lapse again; `once` would mail them only ever once.

## Tuning

The 90-day and 365-day windows are in the segment condition; change them there, not in the journey. The default waits five days between the two messages.
checklist: Confirm the conversion event name (`Order Completed`) your site sends.
Check the 90-day and 365-day windows with your sales cycle.
Replace or remove the offer code; an empty code still mentions the code in the second e-mail, so edit that line if there is no offer.
Keep the unsubscribe and preference links in both e-mails.
Publish the segment first, then the templates and the journey, or submit them together.
Check the audience count with segments.preview before publishing the journey.
